description:
Channel registry (web, POS, presale, reseller) with per-channel price/fee rules and sales windows; presale/unlock codes; external reseller API selling from shared inventory.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A channel = allocation + price/fee rules + window, all overridable per TKT-5 hierarchy
- Presale codes gate access to configured windows
- Reseller API sells from shared inventory with the same no-oversell guarantee and per-reseller attribution

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⚠️ Decomposition readiness — CONCERNS

Decomposed into six vertical slices (TKT-235 … TKT-240), ordered by dependency.

| Child | Slice | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| TKT-235 | US-CH1 Channel registry (catalog table + CRUD + reads) | — |
| TKT-236 | US-CH2 Back-office channel + allocation administration | 235 |
| TKT-237 | US-CH3 Per-channel price rules (the axis fees already have) | 235 |
| TKT-238 | US-CH4 Per-channel sales windows (claim-time, clock_timestamp()) | 235 |
| TKT-239 | US-CH5 Presale unlock codes (gated-channel access) | 235, 238 |
| TKT-240 | US-CH6 Reseller API (partner identity + seam closure) | 235, 237, 238 |

**What was already shipped, and therefore is not in scope here:** channel allocations with caps and scheduled release (TKT-78 / ADR-024), per-channel *fee* rules (TKT-214 / ADR-046) and per-channel split schedules (TKT-216 / ADR-047). Each of those tickets deferred the registry, pricing, windows and reseller work to TKT-17 by name; this decomposition is the redemption of those deferrals.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Sizing | ✅ | Six slices, each end-to-end and independently demoable; none is a horizontal layer |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | TKT-235 (registry) is the prefactor; everything else hangs off it |
| Ordered by dependency | ✅ | No forward dependencies; cycle check walked — none |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Every COS names a test or an observable refusal |
| Dependencies wired | ✅ | `blocked-by` links set on 236, 237, 238, 239, 240 |
| Context-mémo baked | ✅ | Per child, `governingAdrs` populated from docs/adr/ by area; every cited ADR verified to resolve at HEAD |
| Quality gates | ✅ | `make check` on all; `make browser` additionally on TKT-236 (web-UI write forms) |
| No unvalidated assumption | ⚠️ | See concerns 1–3 |

**Concerns:**
1. **TKT-240 introduces a third identity class** (machine-to-machine partner credential) on an externally reachable surface. ADR-043 decides *where* the guard lives; the credential *shape* is an open design decision that would normally be `owner: human` and hold at Gate 1.
2. **TKT-240 closes the commerce→inventory channel seam, which is an intended breaking change** — some reserves that succeed today will return 409. It is documented as deliberate at `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:260-263`, so closing it is a product decision, not a defect fix.
3. **TKT-237 and TKT-239 touch money and the contention hot path** respectively, with data migrations on both.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — structurally sound and ready to run, with three named risks concentrated in TKT-237/239/240. Under normal operation this verdict asks the owner to clear Gate 1 eyes-open. On this run the owner has explicitly waived the gates and reaffirmed after being shown concerns 1–3 by name; the children proceed on that waiver, and every objection overridden downstream is recorded in each child's `kind=metrics` `overrides:` list.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Epic closeout — TKT-17: Sales channels & reseller API

All **12** children Done. Closed on the epic's own COS, each checked against shipped code rather
than against the children being green.

#### COS

| COS | verdict |
|---|---|
| *A channel = allocation + price/fee rules + window, all overridable per the TKT-5 hierarchy* | **met** — registry (TKT-235), fees (pre-existing) + price axis (TKT-237), windows (TKT-238, ADR-054), allocations (ADR-024), all resolved through ADR-036's scope hierarchy |
| *Presale codes gate access to configured windows* | **met** — TKT-239, ADR-055 (`requires_code`), judged under the pool row lock |
| *Reseller API sells from shared inventory with the same no-oversell guarantee and per-reseller attribution* | **met** — TKT-240 (API), TKT-246 (`sold_by` binding, judged under the pool lock), attribution persisted on reservation/order/claim |

#### Children

`TKT-235` `TKT-236` `TKT-237` `TKT-238` `TKT-239` `TKT-240` — the six US-CH stories.
`TKT-241` `TKT-243` `TKT-244` `TKT-246` `TKT-248` `TKT-250` — follow-ups, five of them raised by
adversarial review of a sibling.

**Span:** epic created 2026-07-12, entered Ready 2026-08-09, first child that day, last child
(TKT-248) merged 2026-08-17. **Active build: 9 days.**

`diff:` n/a at epic level — carried by the children.
`human-wait total:` n/a (children ran under `gates: autonomous`; Gate 1 and several design
decisions were the owner's).

#### overrides:

**none at the epic level.** Each child recorded its own; the two that carried residual risk say so
in their closeouts (TKT-244's unquantified residual at the churn cap; TKT-248's unreviewed pass-3
commit `2281c62c`).

#### learnings:

The epic's dominant theme, and it took five follow-up tickets to learn it:

1. **A channel is an authorization axis, not a routing label.** TKT-240 shipped the forward, was
   **reverted** after its own review, and the closure then took three more tickets (TKT-246, TKT-248,
   plus TKT-244's credential). The rule that emerged — *making a request field load-bearing is an
   authorization change* — is already promoted to `AGENTS.md`.
2. **The guard belongs where the decision is.** Inventory judges seller/code/window/capacity under
   the pool row lock; catalog judges entitlement at resolve time. A check in the calling service
   binds only callers who go through it. (ADR-024 amendments, ADR-060.)
3. **Lookup ≠ constraint, and the distinction survived three tickets that could have broken it.**
   The registry never gates a sale; TKT-241 bought the end-to-end guard, and TKT-248 narrowed it
   without overturning it. Recorded in ADR-024/ADR-060 and pinned by
   `smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go`.
4. **Vacuous tests were the epic's most expensive defect class** — TKT-241 existed *entirely* to fix
   them, and TKT-248 still shipped three more. Promoted to
   `docs/learnings/2026-08-17-a-test-that-restates-its-helper.md`.

All four are already in `AGENTS.md`, an ADR, or `docs/learnings/`. **No further promotion owed.**

#### retro:

**(1) What would have made this epic faster or better?**

- **TKT-240 was the expensive lesson and it was avoidable.** It shipped a forward from an
  unauthenticated route, was reverted after review, and cost a full build-review-revert cycle plus
  three follow-up tickets. The signal was present at shaping: the route was already known to be
  unauthenticated. *Concrete change, already applied:* the "enumerate every producer of the value
  and ask which are authenticated" rule is in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Five of twelve children were review-raised follow-ups.** That is not waste — it is the review
  working — but it means the epic's real size was roughly double its planned size. Worth knowing
  when sizing the next authorization-shaped epic.

**(2) What should the humans change?**

- **Two seams were deliberately left open and are now the epic's residual**, both recorded and
  neither hidden: **TKT-176** (seated claims ignore allocations — now unreachable by any route,
  description amended 2026-08-17) and the **historical-row exchange repricing** note in ADR-060.
  Neither blocks anything; both should be decided before a seated event sells through a reseller.
- **The `ADR-055` number is used twice** (`presale-unlock-codes` and `on-sale-write-rate-limiting`).
  Cite by filename. Flagged during TKT-248 shaping and still unfixed — it is a one-line registry
  hygiene fix nobody owns.
